extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models with texture-specific prompts and a three-stage refinement process consisting of frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Texture images were generated using Stable Diffusion text-to-image models based on constructed prompts. Prompts were created by combining descriptive words across categories (artistic, spatial, color enhancer, color, texture) to produce 96,768 unique prompts. Five images were generated per prompt, resulting in 483,840 initial images before refinement.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were generated from text prompts using the Stable Diffusion model from HuggingFace. The texture classes were based on 47 texture classes from the Describable Textures Dataset (DTD) plus 9 additional texture classes sourced from additional lists of textures, resulting in 56 total texture classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering to remove object-like images by retaining the top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values based on Fourier transforms; (2) Patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images by filtering out the bottom 20% of images with lowest mean patch variance (50x50 pixel patches); (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure prompt alignment by filtering out the bottom 20% of images with lowest CLIP scores within each texture class. This reduced the dataset from 483,840 images to 246,285 images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was conducted with 9 participants who evaluated 100 images each (900 unique images total). Participants rated each image on two questions: (1) overall quality of the image, and (2) how well the image represents the provided descriptor. Ratings were provided on a scale of 1 to 5, with 1 being the worst and 5 being the best.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation scores were analyzed at different stages of the refinement process to validate that each refinement step improved quality and representativeness. Results showed a 3.4% increase in quality and 4.5% increase in representativeness overall through the refinement process. CLIP scores were found to align well with human representative scores.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each of the 900 evaluated images received 1 human annotation consisting of two ratings (quality and representativeness).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) was used to compute alignment scores between images and text prompts. Inception model was used for computing Inception Scores. Fourier transforms were used for frequency analysis.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables research on texture bias in machine learning models, which has implications for understanding model interpretability, uncovering biases, and identifying security vulnerabilities. The dataset has been used to develop Texture Object Association Values (TAV), a metric that measures texture bias by quantifying how predictions change in the presence of different textures.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The NSFW safety filter in Stable Diffusion flagged up to 60% of initially generated images, with certain texture descriptors like 'paisley' consistently triggering the filter despite containing no explicit content. This indicates the safety filter may be overly sensitive to texture-based content. Flagged images were excluded from the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: More structured textures such as grid and polka-dotted textures tend to have worse Inception and FID scores compared to textures that commonly appear in objects (e.g., hairy, flaky). Certain descriptor combinations (e.g., 'muted', 'earthy' paired with subtle textures like 'gauzy' and 'veined') result in lower quality images. The dataset is generated synthetically and may not capture all characteristics of real-world textures.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for texture-based research including: understanding high-level features models learn, uncovering biases, identifying security vulnerabilities, measuring texture bias in models, constructing texture-object associations, and creating adversarial examples. It has been used to develop Texture Object Association Values (TAV) for measuring texture bias in object classification models.
